title: OS course: xv6
intro: xv6 is the small teaching Unix used in MIT 6.1810. The 2026 labs are cloned in ~/xv6-labs-2026 and run here with the course's own Makefile and grader. If that folder is missing you're on the previous system version: press Reset first.

steps.text: Go to the lab. It starts on branch util, the first lab.
Build and boot xv6. It takes about 10 seconds, then xv6's own shell shows a $ prompt.
You're in xv6 now, not Debian. List its files: every user program is one file.
Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>A</kbd>, then <kbd>x</kbd>, to stop xv6 and return to Debian. Then tick this step.
A user program is a C file in user/. Read echo.c: your first exercise, sleep, looks much like it.
New programs are added to UPROGS in the Makefile. Write user/sleep.c with nano, then add $U/_sleep here.
Run the grader for one test. It fails until sleep works, and tells you why.
Debug the kernel: start xv6 waiting for a debugger. Tick this step when it says Now run gdb.
Open a second shell with + above the terminal.
In the new tab, attach gdb and stop at the kernel's main. No + button? Press Reset to get the version with tabs.
steps.cmd: cd ~/xv6-labs-2026 && gdb -q -nx -ex 'set confirm off' -ex 'set architecture riscv:rv64' -ex "target remote 127.0.0.1:$(make -s print-gdbport)" -ex 'symbol-file kernel/kernel' -ex 'break main' -ex continue

steps.text: Where are we? Show the call stack.
Step over a few lines of main.
Back in the console tab, xv6 has stopped and the prompt is back.
Other labs are branches: syscall, pgtbl, traps, cow, mmap. Commit your work before you switch. More help: cat ~/xv6-README.txt.
